```python
def prefix_tokens(values, prefix):
    # values: sorted unique feasible target values (all matching prefix)
    chars = np.zeros(10, dtype=bool)
    end = False
    m = len(prefix)
    if m == 0:
        end = False  # no spelling is empty
    else:
        target = int(prefix)
        if str(target) == prefix:
            end = bool((values == target).any())
    for L in range(1, 8):
        low = 0 if L == 1 else 10**(L-1)
        high = 9 if L == 1 else 10**L - 1
        sel = (values >= low) & (values <= high)
        if not sel.any(): continue
        sub = values[sel]
        if L == m:
            continue  # END handled above
        if L < m: continue  # cannot have a next char (already filtered: these can't match prefix)
        # next char is digit at position m
        shift = 10 ** (L - m - 1)
        digits = (sub // shift) % 10
        chars[digits] = True
    tokens = [str(d) for d in range(10) if chars[d]]
    if end: tokens.append('END')
    return tokens
```

old = '''def prefix_tokens(values: np.ndarray, prefix: str) -> list[str]:
    """Next tokens, in protocol order ``"0".."9"`` then ``"END"``."""
    tokens = [digit for digit in DIGITS if _spelling_exists(values, prefix + digit)]
    if _spelling_equals(values, prefix):
        tokens.append("END")
    return tokens
'''
new = '''def prefix_tokens(values: np.ndarray, prefix: str) -> list[str]:
    """Next tokens of ``values`` after ``prefix``, as ``"0".."9"`` then ``"END"``.

    Every value in ``values`` already starts with ``prefix``, so a value with
    more digits than ``prefix`` contributes the digit at that position and a
    value with exactly ``len(prefix)`` digits contributes ``"END"``.
    """
    present = np.zeros(10, dtype=bool)
    length = len(prefix)
    if length and _spelling_equals(values, prefix):
        present_end = True
    else:
        present_end = False
    for digits in range(max(1, length), 8):
        low = 0 if digits == 1 else 10 ** (digits - 1)
        high = 9 if digits == 1 else 10 ** digits - 1
        if digits == length:
            continue
        selected = (values >= low) & (values <= high)
        if not selected.any():
            continue
        shift = 10 ** (digits - length - 1)
        present[(values[selected] // shift) % 10] = True
    tokens = [DIGITS[digit] for digit in range(10) if present[digit]]
    if present_end:
        tokens.append("END")
    return tokens
'''
assert old in t
t = t.replace(old, new)
p.write_text(t)
print('ok')
